claims.title: Local-memory certificates and reusable boundary intervention under actuation limits

quoted_fields.interface: The producer completes a finite local-forgetting certificate for a declared interacting transport class, then reuses retained probe and isolated-control data to certify a later combined intervention without new calibration. A completed two-actuator native simulation delivered positive net particles, but used 5.34 times more chemical input per delivered particle than the three-actuator window. The result is reusable prediction under an actuation constraint, not an energy-saving or completed physical device.
quoted_fields.failure: Three-source production used4.61567kBT chemical input per net particle; the pair used24.64874kBT, a5.34x penalty. The inactive source stayed connected to the background bath and drained290991 particles. All three actuators and four baseline contacts remained installed, and earlier phases used all three sources. The last window limits simultaneous added-birth actuation; it establishes neither installed-hardware nor energy saving. Detector energy, switching work, clocks, computation, erasure, fabrication, external reservoir preparation and final reset remain unpriced. No conversion of model time/site count to seconds/fabricated area is supplied. Physical implementation remains unresolved; no complete-device efficiency or industrial-throughput claim follows.
